description: Use this right after `search_families`, to show the user the Families you recommend. Not for Sets or icons the user already chose. Next: `search_assets` with the chosen Family's `set.slug` as `setSlug`. Shows your recommendation as a preview: each Family drawn with sample icons for the user's product, which they compare and choose from. Pass 3 Families, best first, with slugs exactly as `search_families` returned them, a short reason for each, and the icons the product needs. Pass fewer only when the user named the Family they want or `search_families` returned fewer. Call it directly after `search_families`: it needs no `get_all_sets_from_family` call first. The icons are samples: this is a recommendation, and you can still choose other icons later. Where the preview is displayed, reply in one or two sentences with your pick and the next step, without listing the Families again. Clients that display no preview, such as terminals, get the same picks as data: present them yourself as a short list with their links.

concepts.description: The sample icons to draw, 4 to 8. Each is `{label, query}`: `label` is the user's word ("Straight razor"), and `query` is what the icon search receives: the one or two words an icon would be named, because every word has to match ("razor", not "straight razor"). A plain string is both. When the user named icons, use their words as labels; otherwise choose what the product will obviously need (a calm finance app: wallet, piggy bank, credit card, pie chart). Omit when the question describes no product, and common interface icons are drawn.

families.description: The Families you recommend, best fit first: 3, unless the user named the Family they want or `search_families` returned fewer. The first is marked as the best fit.

set.description: The Set to open this Family on: its `slug` from `sampleSets`, or its name. Omit to open on its first Set.

slug.description: Family slug, exactly as `search_families` returned it.

why.description: One short sentence, under 80 characters, on why this Family fits the product, in visual terms the user can see: shape, stroke, corners, tone. Shown under the Family name.

name: show_families_preview
title: Show Families preview
